commands_used: answer 1. I carry three seal-stones that open the Kings' Gate, which guards the Eye of Argonia under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire. The Eye can heal the sick Hist trees. A rival, the Collector Ennodius Vanin, is also after it. 2. Bring the three stones to Never-Writes-Twice at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom. 3. I can go straight to Never-Writes-Twice and hand over the stones, or talk first to ask questions. I have not yet seen other choices. 4. I do not understand why the Unbound seal trees, what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or how Nesh-Deeka knows of the Unbound. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice.

answer 1. Never-Writes-Twice made me Ka-Deelith of the Toh-Reel-Ka and gave me a pike and armour. The Unbound are not yet near Teku-Sul, so I am ahead of them. 2. Dive to Teku-Sul Spire and go to the Kings' Gate, set the three stones, and use the Eye where it sits to heal the trees without lifting it. Then take the stones back to her and hunt Cuts-the-Old-Knot. 3. I can go to the gate now; later I decide how to deal with the Eye. I have been told not to lift it. 4. I do not know why the Unbound seal trees, what is in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or how Nesh-Deeka knows the Unbound. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice.

answer 1. Cuts-the-Old-Knot waits at the Kings' Gate. She says the Toh-Reel-Ka keep sap-fed dreamers in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar to watch the marsh through the trees, that she was one, and that Never-Writes-Twice lied. She seals trees so the dreamers cannot see. Using the Eye in place heals all trees but keeps the dreams; lifting it ends the dreams and kills about three in ten trees. 2. Choose here: fight her or believe her. 3. Fight her and go on alone, or believe her so she fights the guardian beside me. The final choice at the Eye stays mine either way. 4. I cannot verify her claims, and I do not know what the guardian is. I could learn more at the gate.

answer 1. I chose to believe Cuts-the-Old-Knot over Never-Writes-Twice. She will fight the guardian beside me beyond the gate. I have promised her nothing about the Eye. 2. Set the three seal-stones in the Kings' Gate at the sunken ruin. 3. After the gate, I decide at the Eye whether to use it in place (heals all trees, dreams continue) or lift it (ends the dreams, about three in ten trees die). I would still need to weigh both. 4. I do not know what the guardian is, and I cannot confirm whether the dreamer story is true. I could check the Fort Chalkmoth cellar.

answer Notes: I took the three seal-stones (Blackrose, Gemin, Vorannuhl) to Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom. She made me Ka-Deelith of the Toh-Reel-Ka and gave me the pike, gauntlets and boots. At the sunken ruin (Teku-Sul) Cuts-the-Old-Knot met me without stones. She says the order keeps sap-fed dreamers in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar and sees the marsh through them, and that Never-Writes-Twice kept the key and lied. I chose to believe her and not fight her. She will fight the guardian beside me past the gate. I still carry the stones, Eye-Setting, Keystone, gold, poison and the rest. Next is to set the stones in the Kings' Gate. The final choice is mine at the Eye: use it in place (heals every tree, dreams continue) or lift it (ends the dreams, about three in ten trees die, the order breaks). I promised Cuts nothing about the Eye. I could not verify her claims. Unknown: what the guardian is and what is truly in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar.
